# Patches on third-party code

Every change that ipcam makes to vendored third-party code is listed here, one entry per patch, so that a rebase onto a new upstream release can redo each one and check it with its test. An entry says what changes, why, which files it touches, which test covers it, and its rebase status.

## MediaMTX (`mediamtx/`)

Upstream: `github.com/bluenviron/mediamtx` (MIT), vendored by `tools/scripts/vendor-mediamtx.sh`. The version, commit and checksums are in [`mediamtx/SOURCE.md`](mediamtx/SOURCE.md). The fork is a nested module outside `ipcam/go.work` (ruling C03), so every command below runs in `hub/third_party/mediamtx` with `GOWORK=off`:

- build: `GOWORK=off go build -o <bin>/mediamtx .`
- patch tests and the recorder's own tests: `GOWORK=off go test -run '^TestMTX' ./...` and `GOWORK=off go test ./internal/recorder/...`

The other upstream tests are not run. Some of them fail in the fork because of MTX-0 (see below).

**Upstream tests changed.** Besides the adaptations that each patch lists, one upstream test of the recorder is changed only to make it reliable:

- `TestRecorderFMP4NegativeInitialDTS` (`internal/recorder/recorder_test.go`) waited a fixed 50 ms between writing its units and closing the recorder. `Close` drops the units still in the recorder's queue, so on a loaded runner the last audio unit could be lost and with it the part that the test reads: it failed once in CI (PR run 40219718421), and 2 of 200 runs with `-race` on a core shared with `stress-ng`. It now waits, for at most 10 s, for the disk writer's second fsync request (MTX-1's `syncAsked` seam), which only the last unit causes; 600 runs under the same load passed. **Rebase:** redo it while upstream's test still sleeps; it needs MTX-1's seam.

**Rebasing.** `tools/scripts/vendor-mediamtx.sh <tag>` replaces the upstream tree (`main.go`, `internal/`, `LICENSE`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`) and applies MTX-0. It stops when one of MTX-0's anchors has moved. Then `GOWORK=off go mod tidy`, redo the dependency changes below that the new release still needs, update `SOURCE.md`, and redo MTX-1… from the diff of their commits, each with its test.

### Dependency versions that differ from upstream's go.mod

- `golang.org/x/net` v0.59.0 → v0.60.0, by `GOWORK=off go get golang.org/x/net@v0.60.0 && GOWORK=off go mod tidy`.
  - **Why.** The security exception to the 14-day rule (ruling R09). govulncheck finds GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6612 and GO-2026-6617 (HTTP/2 in `net/http`) reachable from the fork, through the WHIP client and the packet dumper. All five are fixed in v0.60.0, which was published on 2026-10-08 and was 12 days old on 2026-10-20. Its requirements are versions the fork already uses.
  - **Files touched.** `go.mod`, `go.sum`.
  - **Test.** The fork's govulncheck step in `ipcam-spike-recording.yml`.
  - **Rebase status.** MediaMTX v1.21.2 still requires v0.59.0, so a re-vendor to it redoes this change. Drop it once upstream requires v0.60.0 or later.
- `require github.com/AndreiBesliu/DevWorld/ipcam/hub v0.0.0` (resolved by MTX-0's `replace`), `filippo.io/age` v1.3.2 (MTX-2's tests) and `go` 1.26.0 → 1.27.2, by `GOWORK=off go mod tidy` once MTX-2 imports `hub/internal/crypto`, then `v0.0.0` in place of the pseudo-version that tidy writes for a replaced module.
  - **Why.** MTX-2 encrypts with the hub's own age writer (C03, C04). The hub module declares `go 1.27.2`, so the fork, which requires it, must too. The versions it brings (`filippo.io/age` v1.3.2, `filippo.io/hpke` v0.4.0, `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.57.0) are the hub's. The hub's module graph also raises the test-only `github.com/rogpeppe/go-internal` (through `kr/pretty`) from v1.14.1 to v1.16.0 in `go.sum`.
  - **Files touched.** `go.mod`, `go.sum`.
  - **Test.** Every MTX-2 test imports `hub/internal/crypto`; the fork's govulncheck and license steps in `ipcam-spike-recording.yml` cover the new modules.
  - **Rebase status.** Redo with `GOWORK=off go mod tidy` after the re-vendor, and set the hub's requirement back to `v0.0.0`.
- `github.com/bluenviron/mediacommon/v2` v2.9.5 → v2.9.6 and `github.com/mattn/go-isatty` v0.0.23 → v0.0.24, plus the indirect `modernc.org/sqlite` v1.60.1, `modernc.org/libc` v1.77.1, `modernc.org/mathutil` v1.7.1, `modernc.org/memory` v1.12.1, `github.com/dustin/go-humanize` v1.0.1, `github.com/ncruces/go-strftime` v1.0.0 and `github.com/remyoudompheng/bigfft` v0.0.0-20230129092748-24d4a6f8daec, by `GOWORK=off go mod tidy` once the fork's tests import `hub/internal/recorder` (Task 5).
  - **Why.** `TestMTX0_AcceptsHubGeneratedConfig` and `TestMTX2_SmallPartMatchesRecorder` check the hub's recorder against the fork. The hub requires mediacommon v2.9.6, the video spike's version (Global Constraints, the shared build list), and its catalog requires modernc.org/sqlite, whose requirements bring go-isatty v0.0.24 and the rest. Minimal version selection takes them into the fork's build list, the binary's included: only mediacommon reaches its code, and v2.9.6 is the version that MediaMTX v1.21.2 requires (its changes: an H.264 picture after an SEI recovery point now counts as a random access point, and its rewindable reader keeps no empty read).
  - **Files touched.** `go.mod`, `go.sum`.
  - **Test.** The fork's patch tests and its recorder tests in the `recorder` and `windows` jobs; the fork's govulncheck and license steps cover the new modules (all BSD-3-Clause or MIT).
  - **Rebase status.** Redo with `GOWORK=off go mod tidy` after the re-vendor; v1.21.2 already requires mediacommon v2.9.6.

### MTX-0: own module path, no rpiCamera source, committed go:generate outputs

- **What.**
  1. **Module path.** The module is renamed from `github.com/bluenviron/mediamtx` to `github.com/AndreiBesliu/DevWorld/ipcam/hub/third_party/mediamtx`, and every quoted import of the old path is rewritten. That also covers the package prefix that `internal/apidocsgen` matches on. URLs of the upstream project (the `upgrade` command, comments) are left alone. `go.mod` gets `replace github.com/AndreiBesliu/DevWorld/ipcam/hub => ../..`; the matching `require` came with MTX-2, the first patch that imports `hub/internal/crypto` (`go mod tidy` drops a requirement that nothing imports yet, and keeps the replace). The rewrite, as the script runs it:

     ```bash
     grep -rlZF --include='*.go' '"github.com/bluenviron/mediamtx/' . \
       | xargs -0 sed -i 's|"github.com/bluenviron/mediamtx/|"github.com/AndreiBesliu/DevWorld/ipcam/hub/third_party/mediamtx/|g'
     go mod edit -module github.com/AndreiBesliu/DevWorld/ipcam/hub/third_party/mediamtx \
       -replace github.com/AndreiBesliu/DevWorld/ipcam/hub=../..
     ```

     Imports are not re-sorted (no `gofmt`), so the rewrite stays a pure substitution.
  2. **No rpiCamera.** The Raspberry Pi camera source is removed:
     - its package `internal/staticsources/rpicamera` is deleted;
     - its registration is removed: the import and the `case s.Conf.Source == "rpiCamera":` of `internal/staticsources/handler.go`, which is where `internal/core`'s paths create their static sources;
     - the `rpiCamera` case of `internal/conf/path.go` now returns `source 'rpiCamera' is not supported: this build has no Raspberry Pi camera source` instead of validating the camera's settings, so a configuration that asks for the source is rejected when it loads, before a path could reach the handler's `panic("should not happen")`.

     The `rpiCamera*` fields of `conf.Path` stay, so a configuration that only sets them still parses. The constant `defs.APIPathSourceTypeRPICameraSource` and the field copies in `internal/core/path_manager.go` also stay; they are inert.
  3. **Generated files.** The module zip lacks the outputs of MediaMTX's `go:generate` steps, so they are committed:
     - `internal/servers/hls/hls.min.js`: `dist/hls.min.js` of the hls.js release that `internal/servers/hls/hlsjsdownloader/VERSION` names. The script downloads its `release.zip` and checks it against `hlsjsdownloader/HASH`, as upstream's downloader does.
     - `internal/core/VERSION`: the tag, without a line break, as upstream's `versiongetter` writes `git describe --tags`.

     The `go:generate` directives and their generator programs stay unchanged.
- **Why.**
  - C03: the fork needs a module path under `…/ipcam/hub/` to import `hub/internal/crypto` (MTX-2), and its own module keeps MediaMTX's ~100 requirements out of `hub/go.mod` and out of the workspace build list.
  - R05: the rpiCamera source embeds prebuilt `mtxrpicam` binaries that link LGPL libcamera into the Pi builds, where go-licenses cannot see them. The hub never uses a CSI camera.
  - C02: `go build` needs `hls.min.js` and `VERSION` for `go:embed`; committing them keeps the build offline and reproducible. Their SHA-256 and content are in `SOURCE.md`.
- **Files touched.**
  - `go.mod` (module line, replace).
  - Every `.go` file with an import of the old path (283 files on v1.21.1, substitution only).
  - `internal/staticsources/rpicamera/` (deleted).
  - `internal/staticsources/handler.go`, `internal/conf/path.go`.
  - `internal/servers/hls/hls.min.js`, `internal/core/VERSION` (added).
- **Test.** `mtx0_test.go`:
  - `TestMTX0_NoUpstreamImportPath`: no `.go` file imports the old path, whatever its build tags, and `go.mod` names the fork's path.
  - `TestMTX0_NoRpiCameraSource`: the package is gone, no file refers to it, and `conf.Load` rejects `source: rpiCamera` while it accepts the same file with an RTSP source.
  - `TestMTX0_GeneratedFilesMatchSourceMD`: the SHA-256 of `hls.min.js` and the content of `VERSION` are the ones `SOURCE.md` records, and `VERSION` names the vendored tag. `ipcam/.gitattributes` marks the fork `-text`, so that a Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf`) keeps those bytes and the `windows` job runs these tests too.
  - `TestMTX0_AcceptsHubGeneratedConfig` (`internal/conf/hubconfig_test.go`): the configuration that ipcam-hub writes (`hub/internal/recorder.GenerateConfig`) loads through this loader and its validation, for a clear job, scoped jobs with the padding on and off, all three together and no job, with every server off, each path pulling over TCP and recording fMP4 with ipcam's `recordPath`, `recordDeleteAfter` 0, the recipients, the padding and the hook command that the hub meant.

  Upstream tests that MTX-0 breaks, and that the fork does not run: the rpiCamera cases of `TestConfErrors` (`internal/conf`); `TestDefaultConfFile` and `internal/linters/conf`, which read `mediamtx.yml` from the upstream root, a file the fork does not vendor.
- **Rebase status.** Applied by `vendor-mediamtx.sh` on v1.21.1 (2026-10-20). Ruling C1-R8 keeps v1.21.1 for the spike, so MTX-1 and MTX-3 are built on it. The fork moves to v1.21.2 only if that release's changelog carries a fix to the recorder path or a security fix (checked before the release, in Task 13), by the rebase procedure above.

### MTX-1: `.part` naming, fsync and rename

- **What.** Upstream writes an fMP4 segment under its final name and never fsyncs it: there is no `.part` name, no rename and no fsync of the file or of its directory. MTX-1 introduces all of them, for fMP4 segments, and takes the segments' disk work off MediaMTX's recording goroutine:
  1. **Naming.** A segment is created as `<recordPath>.mp4.part` and renamed to `<recordPath>.mp4` when it closes. `OnSegmentCreate` (and so `runOnRecordSegmentCreate`) gets the `.part` path, the file that exists while the segment is written. MTX-2 adds `.mp4.age.part` → `.mp4.age`.
  2. **The disk writer.** The recording goroutine (the reader's callbacks) never touches the disk. It marshals each part, with the segment's init before its first part, and hands it to the recorder's disk writer (`diskWriter` in `diskwriter.go`): a goroutine of its own that creates, writes and closes the segments in the order it gets them. The parts wait in memory until it writes them, at most `maxQueuedBytes` per recorder: 8 MiB (C1-R17), 16 s of a 4 Mbps stream, which covers the 12.7 s stalls measured in Task 7.2d; with 8 cameras on a Pi 5 the worst case is about 72 MiB. Past that the recording waits for the disk, as upstream's does, and MediaMTX's reader queue discards the frames that do not fit and logs them ("reader is too slow, discarding N frames"), as for any slow reader: each frame that the bound makes it discard is counted in those lines, and no part is torn. Once a segment's file is closed, the disk writer logs at Info `[recorder] disk queue peak: <n> bytes`, the most bytes of parts that it held since the previous such line, the part being written included; the hub's load test (MI3, Task 9) reads these lines against §4.8's RAM budgets. A disk that is slow for seconds, an fsync or a directory sync waiting behind another writer's data, then holds up neither the recording nor MediaMTX's reader queue (`writeQueueSize`, 512 RTP packets, about 1.5 s of a 4 Mbps stream), which would discard every frame past it (Task 7.2d).
  3. **Every part.** A part's fsync is requested when the part is written (for an encrypted segment, padded and flushed: MTX-2), before the next part's first write, and it runs in order beside the recording (C1-R17): on the segment's part syncer (`partSyncer` in `syncer.go`), a goroutine of its own, one fsync per part, while the disk writer goes on writing. On a disk that syncs in milliseconds each part is durable before the next one is written, as before Task 7.2d. On a slow disk a part is durable once its fsync returns, and the parts written after it wait in the page cache.
  4. **Creation.** The disk writer creates a segment's `.part` with its first part, and only once the segment before it is closed (5.): ipcam-hub's part watcher takes a `.part` that a newer `.part` of its stream follows for one that MediaMTX has left, and repairs it (`hub/internal/recorder/status.go`, `leftBehind`), so a newer `.part` must not appear while an older one is still being closed. The directory sync that makes the new name durable is the first job of the segment's part syncer, ahead of every part's fsync, so a part whose fsync has returned is in a file whose name is durable. `OnSegmentCreate` runs right after the creation, so before that directory sync has returned (C1-R17); ipcam-hub does not use it.
  5. **Close, in this order**, on the disk writer: the part syncer's last fsync, the last write (for a clear segment, the duration in `mvhd`, written into the `.part` before the rename), one more file fsync, `Close`, the rename, the directory sync, and then MTX-3's hook. Without the last fsync, the directory sync could make the final name durable while the file's last bytes are still in the page cache (ext4's delayed allocation does not force them out on a rename to a new name). Only then does the disk writer create the next segment's file; meanwhile the next segment's parts wait in memory (2.).
  6. **What a stop loses** (C1-R17, C1-R18). Parts wait in memory (2.) only while the disk writer is held: by a segment's close (5.), by the next segment's creation (4.: creating its directory (MkdirAll), its file, and then an encrypted segment's age header or a clear segment's init), or by a part's write that blocks, as a write does when the system throttles writers while the disk falls behind (Linux's dirty-page throttling). A slow part fsync does not hold it (3.) until the segment's close waits for it (5.).
     - **A process crash** (kill -9) while the disk writer is not held loses at most the part being recorded. The parts written before it are in the page cache, which outlives the process, also while their fsyncs wait on a slow disk.
     - **A power cut** loses, besides, the parts whose fsync has not returned. On a responsive disk that is the part being written, which HUB-07 counts. During a disk stall it is about the stall's length: the same seconds that the recorder discarded as frames before Task 7.2d, when it waited for each fsync.
     - **C1-R18, deferred to Faza 1: a kill -9 while the disk writer is held** loses, besides, the parts held in memory: about the hold's length, at most the bound (2.), the same seconds that the recording discarded as frames before Task 7.2d, when it waited for the disk itself. C1-R18 names a segment's close stalled on a slow disk: the disk writer creates the next segment's file only after that close (4.), so the next segment's parts are not in any file yet, and fixing that needs a hub live-repair rule with a flagged MTX-3 hook or a staging name, both changes of approved contracts. A stalled creation of the next segment's file and a throttled write lose parts the same way. Faza 1's recorder design, or HUB-30's plan B, owns all three. MI1's lab and owner runs measure the loss, and an over-limit lab run's `mi1-diag` notice shows which hold it was, by the stream's newest files at the stop (a whole segment of 5 minutes ends with a part whose `seq` is about 300):
       - a `.part` that holds the whole segment: its close was held before the rename;
       - the whole segment under its final name, with no newer file: its close was held in the directory sync after the rename, or the next segment's creation was held before its file appeared;
       - after the whole segment, the next segment's `.part` without a sample, which reconcile removes, so that the notice lists it with size 0 and an error: that creation was held once its file appeared, or its first part's write was throttled before a sample reached the file;
       - a `.part` that ends before the segment's end, seconds before the stop: a part's write was throttled.
  7. **Failures.** The hook runs only for a segment whose every write and sync, `Close`, rename and directory sync succeeded; a write or sync of the segment that failed before its close counts too, which the segment remembers (`partErr`), and such a segment gets no more parts. The disk writer keeps its first failure, and the recording returns it at its next part or segment close, as its own error: the recorder logs it and restarts, as upstream does for any error, about one part later than when the recording wrote the parts itself. The name left on disk depends on the step that failed:
     - a failed write, fsync, `Close` or rename leaves the `.part` name, for the hub's reconcile;
     - so does a failed directory sync after the `.part` is created, which leaves that `.part` with the parts written before the failure was seen;
     - a failed directory sync after a successful rename leaves the final name, without the hook: the hub's reconcile catalogs such a file at its next start (`TestReconcile_CatalogsFinalFilesWithoutRows`).
  8. **Stop.** A recorder that stops, or restarts after an error, first waits until its disk writer has closed every segment it was given, so no segment is left half closed and a restarted recorder's first `.part` comes after them.
  9. **Windows.** The directory sync is a no-op (`dirsync_windows.go`): Windows has no directory fsync and NTFS journals the directory entries. The rename is `MoveFileEx` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING|MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH`, after `Close` (`rename_windows.go`). On other systems the directory is opened and fsynced (`dirsync_other.go`), and the rename is `os.Rename` (`rename_other.go`).
  10. **Seams.** `syncer.go` holds the one-function seams that every call goes through, `syncFile`, `syncDir` and `renameFinal`, so that the tests can count and order the calls; on Windows, `moveFileEx` is a seam too. MTX-2 adds a fourth, `createFile`, and the `segmentFile` interface that `syncFile` takes. `syncAsked` runs when the disk writer asks for a part's fsync, and `diskFailed` (`diskwriter.go`) once the disk writer has noted its first failure; both do nothing, and the tests replace them to see the file at that moment, or to wait for it. `maxQueuedBytes` is a variable so that a test can lower it.

  MPEG-TS segments are unchanged: ipcam records fMP4 only.
- **Why.** Rulings C13 and C14, spec §4.5: a part is durable once its fsync returns, which on a responsive disk is before the next part is written, so that a power cut loses at most the part being written (HUB-07); during a disk stall it loses the parts whose fsync has not returned (6., C1-R17); and the atomic rename means that a final name always points at complete, durable bytes, while an unfinished segment is recognisable by its name for the startup reconcile. The directory is synced at creation and at the rename only, not per part, to keep the fsyncs per open file down (§4.8). The disk work runs beside the recording since Task 7.2d. The MI1 smoke on CI (push run 40242013316) lost 10.85 s of a clear run while the race tests of the same job kept the runner's disk busy. Reproduced on a throttled disk with a background writer, the recorder sat in one part's fsync for up to 12.7 s at the cut while MediaMTX discarded the frames that arrived meanwhile. On that disk a writer that leaves its fsyncs to another thread was measured too: its writes took at most 1 ms while one fsync took 39 s. The same stall could hold the recording at each segment's creation and close (Task 7.2d review, I2), which is why those run on the disk writer too.
- **Files touched.**
  - `internal/recorder/format_fmp4_segment.go`: the recording side (`closeCurPart` and `close` hand the parts and the close to the disk writer) and the disk side (`writePartToDisk`, `create`, `finish`, `fail`), which holds upstream's file code with the `.part` creation, the part syncer, the fsync request after each part, `partErr`, the close order and the disk queue's peak line.
  - `internal/recorder/format_fmp4.go` (the disk writer, `disk` and `writer`, and its stop in `close`).
  - New: `internal/recorder/diskwriter.go`, `syncer.go` (with `partSyncer`), `dirsync_other.go`, `dirsync_windows.go`, `rename_other.go`, `rename_windows.go`.
  - Tests: `internal/recorder/mtx1_test.go`, `mtx1_windows_test.go`.
  - Upstream test adapted: `internal/recorder/recorder_test.go`, where the fMP4 create paths of `TestRecorder` and `TestRecorderFMP4SegmentSwitch` end in `.mp4.part`.
- **Test.** `mtx1_test.go` runs a real `Recorder` (1 s parts, 3 s segments) and wraps the seams, so every call still reaches the disk while the wrapper records what it saw:
  - `TestMTX1_FsyncOnEachPartClose`: a segment of 3 parts gets 4 file fsyncs. Each part's is asked for when the file ends exactly where that part ends, before the next part's first write; they run in that order, and at each the file holds at least its part. The fourth comes after the `mvhd` write, on the open file, and the file does not change after it.
  - `TestMTX1_SlowPartFsyncKeepsRecording`: while the first part's fsync is held, the second part still reaches the file; once it returns, the segment has an fsync per part and closes in the order above.
  - `TestMTX1_SlowSegmentCloseKeepsRecording`: while the first segment's close is held in its fsync, 40 frames of the next segment come through a reader queue of 16, and none is lost. The next `.part` appears only once the first segment has its final name, and the first segment's hook comes before the next segment's creation.
  - `TestMTX1_SlowCreationDirSyncKeepsRecording`: while the directory sync of the creation is held, the first two parts reach the file and no part's fsync runs.
  - `TestMTX1_QueuedPartsAreBounded`: while the creation of the first file is held, a reader queue of 16 loses none of 70 frames; with `maxQueuedBytes` at 1 byte, the recording waits for the disk and frames are lost.
  - `TestMTX1_QueueCapWaitsAndReportsTheDiscards` (C1-R17): `maxQueuedBytes` is 8 MiB. With the bound lowered to two and a half parts (two parts and their boxes fit, a third does not) and the first file's creation held, the third part makes the recording wait; every frame sent is then in a segment, whole and in order, or in MediaMTX's "reader is too slow" lines, or the one sample the recorder holds at its stop; and each closed segment logs its disk queue peak, two parts here, within the bound.
  - `TestMTX1_DirSyncAtCreateAndRenameOnly` (not on Windows): exactly 2 directory syncs, the first when only the `.part` exists and before any part's fsync, the second right after the rename.
  - `TestMTX1_RenameAfterCloseWithFinalName`: while the segment is written only `<name>.mp4.part` exists, afterwards only `<name>.mp4`; the close runs file fsync (file open, `mvhd` written), rename (file closed), directory sync, hook.
  - `TestMTX1_ClearDurationWrittenBeforeRename`: `mvhd` holds the segment's duration in the `.part` at the rename and in the final file.
  - `TestMTX1_FailedPartSyncKeepsPartName`: when the second part's fsync fails, the segment is closed without a rename and without a hook, and only its `.part` is left.
  - `TestMTX1_FailedPartSyncStopsTheRecorderAtTheNextPart`: when the first part's fsync fails, the recorder logs the error at the second part's close, before the segment's end, and the disk writer writes no part into that segment's file after the failure.
  - `TestMTX1_SeamFailureFiresNoHook`: when the close's file fsync, the rename, the directory sync after the rename or the one after the creation fails, no hook runs; the `.part` name is left, except after a successful rename, which leaves the final name.
  - `TestMTX1_WindowsDirSyncNoOpAndWriteThroughRename` (`mtx1_windows_test.go`): the directory sync of a missing directory returns nil, so it opens no handle, and the rename passes `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING|MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH` to `MoveFileEx` and replaces an existing file.

  The `recorder` job of `ipcam-spike-recording.yml` runs them on Linux with `-race`, the `windows` job on windows-latest.
- **Rebase status.** Applied on v1.21.1 (2026-10-20). Re-apply on each adopted MediaMTX release: the new files carry over as they are; in `format_fmp4.go`, add the disk writer and its stop in `close`; in `format_fmp4_segment.go`, split upstream's `closeCurPart` and `close` into the recording side, which marshals the init (with the `.part` path) and each part and sends them, and the disk side, which holds upstream's file code with MTX-1's changes listed under Files touched; then adapt the create paths in `recorder_test.go` and run the tests above.

### MTX-2: age encryption at write

- **What.** A path with age recipients writes its fMP4 segments encrypted with age as they are recorded, so that no clear byte of a recording reaches the disk:
  1. **Configuration** (`internal/conf/path.go`, `age_recipients.go`, `jsonwrapper/unmarshal.go`).
     - `recordAgeRecipients: [<RI_g>, <RK>]`: exactly two different age1 X25519 recipients, checked when the configuration loads with `crypto.ParseKeyScope` (`Path.RecordAgeScope`). Any other value fails the load with an error that never quotes it: one or three entries, a secret key, a hybrid or SSH recipient, RK equal to RI_g, a value that is not a list, an empty list, null (also a YAML key with no value, as a block list whose entries were deleted leaves it), an empty environment variable, or an indexed one (`…_RECORDAGERECIPIENTS_0`). This holds in a path, in `pathDefaults`, from the environment and from the control API. The key needs `recordFormat: fmp4`, since MPEG-TS segments are not encrypted. Only without the key, in the path and in `pathDefaults`, does the path record in clear.
     - The field is `*AgeRecipients` (`internal/conf/age_recipients.go`), nil when the key is absent. A pointer, because `conf.Load` turns every nil slice into an empty one, so a `[]string` could not tell an absent key from an empty list. It holds the two strings, because `Path.Clone` copies settable fields only and would drop the key bytes inside a parsed recipient.
     - Null. MediaMTX reads null as an absent key: `jsonwrapper` sets a pointer to nil on null. `AgeRecipients` implements the new `jsonwrapper.NullRejecter`, so `jsonwrapper` refuses null for it (`cannot set "recordAgeRecipients" to null`); every other key keeps upstream's rule.
     - Environment. `AgeRecipients.UnmarshalEnv` reads one comma-separated variable. An empty variable is an empty list, refused as above; upstream's generic slice loader would panic on it for a nil pointer. A variable whose name only begins with the key's, as an indexed list would, fails the load.
     - `recordAgePadLowBitrate: true|false`, `true` when absent: the per-camera setting O17 („Pierdere minimă la pană de curent”).
     - `internal/core/path.go` passes them to the recorder as `Recorder.AgeScope`, a `*crypto.KeyScope` that holds public keys only, and `Recorder.AgePadLowBitrate`. A changed key recreates the path, since `pathConfCanBeUpdated` compares the whole path configuration.
  2. **Naming.** An encrypted segment is `<recordPath>.mp4.age`, written as `.mp4.age.part` and renamed by MTX-1.
  3. **Strictly in order.** `ageSegmentWriter` (`agewriter.go`) wraps the hub's `crypto.Writer`. It writes the age header for RI_g and RK when the file is created, then the init, each part's `moof` and `mdat`, the padding and the final chunk, all through the writer and in order. At most one chunk of plaintext stays in RAM.
  4. **Padding, per part** (§4.5 as amended by O17). Right after a part is written and before MTX-1 asks for its fsync:
     - `p` is the distance from the part's end in the plaintext to the next 64 KiB chunk boundary; when 0 < p < 8, too short for a free box's header, it is 65,536 bytes more;
     - the part is padded with a `free` box of `p` bytes when the setting is on and the part (its `moof` and `mdat`, without the init or the padding) is shorter than 64 KiB (`smallPartBytes`, equal to `crypto.ChunkSize`), or when `p` is at most 10 % of the part;
     - then `Flush` seals every complete chunk, so that the part's fsync makes everything up to the last chunk boundary durable.

     The decision is per part and keeps no state per stream. The spec's "stream below 512 kbps" is exactly a stream whose parts are under 64 KiB, about 524 kbps with 1 s parts, so the bitrate rule follows from the part size, and a stream whose bitrate varies (night VBR, smart codecs) is padded part by part.
  5. **No seek-back** (C13). The close does not seek back to write the `mvhd` duration of an encrypted segment: its `mvhd` keeps a duration of 0, and playback reads durations from the hub's catalog. The file is only ever appended to.
  6. **Close.** When every byte is sealed already (`Buffered() == 0`, as after a part padded to a boundary), an 8-byte `free` box is written first, so that the final chunk is never empty: age rejects an empty final chunk after other chunks. `Writer.Close` writes the final chunk; MTX-1's close order follows: one more `syncFile`, `Close`, `renameFinal`, `syncDir`, then MTX-3's hook. So the final chunk is durable before the final name.
  7. **Seam.** `createFile` (`syncer.go`) creates the segment file as a `segmentFile`, an interface that `*os.File` implements, so that a test can wrap the file; `syncFile` takes a `segmentFile`.
- **Why.** HUB-04 and C04: no clear frame on disk, with the hub's own age writer (C03). §4.5, R01 and O17 (ruling C1-R1): the `Flush` at every part's fsync bounds what a cut loses to the bytes after the last chunk boundary; padding the small parts keeps a low-bitrate stream within HUB-07 (median ≤ 1 s, maximum ≤ 2 s, with reconcile's whole-sample salvage, R01 and C1-R9) at the cost of disk for that camera only (about twice the bytes at 256 kbps); the 10 % rule aligns a large part when that is cheap. C13: the hub catalogs durations, so the file never needs a seek. C22: a secret key in the configuration is refused without being echoed. `TestMTX2_WorstCaseLoss` prints the loss and disk figures as the `mtx2-loss` notice of the recorder job.
- **Files touched.**
  - New: `internal/recorder/agewriter.go`, `internal/conf/age_recipients.go`.
  - `internal/recorder/format_fmp4_segment.go` (`closeCurPart`, which names the segment `.age`, and MTX-1's disk side: `create`, `writePartToDisk`, `finish`), `syncer.go` (`segmentFile`, `createFile`), `recorder.go` and `recorder_instance.go` (the two settings, at both places where an instance is built).
  - `internal/conf/path.go` (the keys, their default, `RecordAgeScope`, validation), `internal/conf/jsonwrapper/unmarshal.go` (`NullRejecter`), `internal/core/path.go` (`startRecording`).
  - Tests: `internal/recorder/mtx2_test.go`, `mtx2_loss_test.go`, `internal/conf/mtx2_test.go`, `internal/conf/jsonwrapper/mtx2_test.go`, `internal/core/mtx2_test.go`; `internal/recorder/mtx1_test.go` takes `segmentFile` in its seam wrappers.
  - Upstream test adapted: `internal/conf/conf_test.go`, where `TestConfFromFile`'s expected path has `RecordAgePadLowBitrate: true`.
- **Test.** The recorder tests run a real `Recorder` with MTX-1's seam wrappers and decrypt what it wrote:
  - `TestMTX2_EncryptedSegmentHasNoClearFrames` (HUB-04): neither the final file nor the `.part` at any fsync holds the `ftyp` and its brand, a `moof` followed by its `mfhd`, or the first 16 bytes of an SPS, PPS or IDR of the stream (whose NAL units are all at least 16 bytes), while the plaintext holds them; the file decrypts with `crypto.NewRecording(id).OpenReaderAt`, for RI_g and for RK.
  - `TestMTX2_PartBoundaryChunkAligned_WhenPaddingAtMost10Pct`: in a 4 Mbps stream every part follows the 10 % rule and every padded part ends on a chunk boundary; parts sized to need about 20,000 bytes are padded, parts that need about 60,000, over 10 %, are not.
  - `TestMTX2_LowBitrateDecidedPerPart`: with the setting on, a 63 KiB part is aligned and a 65 KiB part is not (HUB-07's boundary), while with it off neither is; in a 450 kbps ± 30 % stream exactly the parts under 64 KiB are aligned by the setting; a 4 Mbps stream follows the 10 % rule only.
  - `TestMTX2_PaddingTooShortForAFreeBoxTakesAChunkMore`: a part that ends 4 bytes before a boundary is padded with 65,540 bytes when the rules pad it.
  - `TestMTX2_FinalChunkSyncedBeforeRename`: the file at the last `syncFile` is the final file, complete for age, with or without the close's free box; `Close`, the rename, the directory sync and the hook follow.
  - `TestMTX2_FlushAtEachPartFsync`: when each part's fsync is asked for, right after the part is written and before the next part's first write, the file is exactly `len(header) + 16 + n·65552` bytes, `n = ⌊plaintext ÷ 65536⌋` of that part's end; at the fsync itself, which runs beside the writes (MTX-1), it holds at least that and is a prefix of the final file.
  - `TestMTX2_NoSeekBack`: an encrypted segment is written and closed, by the next keyframe and by the recorder's stop, through a file that refuses `Read`, `Seek`, `WriteAt` and `Truncate`; a clear segment, the control, does seek.
  - `TestMTX2_FinalChunkNeverEmpty`: a segment whose last part ends on a chunk boundary ends with an 8-byte `free` box in a final chunk of its own, and age decrypts it.
  - `TestMTX2_EncryptedNamingPartThenRename`: only `.mp4.age.part` exists while the segment is written and only `.mp4.age` after; the hooks get these names.
  - `TestMTX2_RestartedRecorderStillEncrypts`: after a failed fsync restarts the recorder, the next segment is encrypted too.
  - `TestMTX2_WorstCaseLoss` (R01, O17): the real part writer runs into a byte-counting sink over 10 minutes of 1 s parts at 20 fps, part sizes uniform within ± 30 %, with MediaMTX's close timing (a part is fsynced one frame after its end, a segment's last part at the next segment's keyframe). At 10,000 uniform cut times, the loss is the cut minus the PTS of the last sample wholly inside the plaintext sealed by the last fsync before it. With the padding on, the median is ≤ 1 s and the maximum ≤ 2 s at 4 Mbps, 450 kbps and 256 kbps, and the disk overhead at 4 Mbps is ≤ 10 %; with it off, the maximum at 256 kbps is ≤ 4 s (§4.5: 1 part + 64 KiB ÷ bitrate, rounded up to whole parts). It prints the figures for 4 Mbps, 512, 450, 384 and 256 kbps as one `mtx2-loss: <json>` line of at most 3,500 bytes once escaped, which the recorder job's `mtx2-loss` step turns into a notice.
  - `TestMTX2_RejectsSecretKeyInRecipients` (C22, `internal/conf`): a secret key as RI_g or RK, one or three recipients, a secret key instead of a list, RI_g as RK, an empty list (also with `mpegts`, and over recipients in `pathDefaults`), null and a key with no value each fail the load, in a path and in `pathDefaults`, with an error that contains no key.
  - `TestMTX2_RejectsEmptyRecipientsFromTheAPI`: a path that the control API adds with an empty list fails validation, and one with null fails to decode. `TestMTX2_RecipientsFromEnv`: one comma-separated variable sets the recipients of a path or of `pathDefaults`; an empty variable (also over recipients that the file sets), one recipient and an indexed variable fail the load. `TestMTX2_CloneKeepsRecipients`: `Conf.Clone` and `Path.Clone` copy the recipients into a list of their own.
  - `TestMTX2_RecipientsNeedFMP4`: the key with `recordFormat: mpegts` fails the load. `TestMTX2_NoRecipientsRecordsInClear`: only without the key, in either format, does the path load with no scope; a path without the key takes `pathDefaults`' recipients.
  - `TestMTX2_NullRejecterBehindPointer` (`internal/conf/jsonwrapper`): null for a `NullRejecter` behind a pointer fails with its key's name, nested too, and leaves the value as it was; a list and `[]` decode; other pointers still take null as nil.
  - `TestMTX2_LowBitratePadding_DefaultOn` and `TestMTX2_LowBitratePadding_Off` (`internal/core`): a MediaMTX core records a 256 kbps RTSP publisher into encrypted segments; with `recordAgePadLowBitrate` absent every part ends on a chunk boundary, with it `false` the parts follow the 10 % rule only.
  - `TestMTX2_ReloadWithOtherRecipientsOrPaddingRecreatesPath` (`internal/core`): a reload that changes a path's recipients or its padding setting, or drops the recipients, recreates the path (`pathConfCanBeUpdated` is false), so its recorder starts again with the new scope; a reload that changes only a `Record*` key that upstream copies is still done in place.
  - `TestMTX2_SmallPartMatchesRecorder` (`internal/recorder/mtx2_const_test.go`): `smallPartBytes` is the hub's `recorder.SmallPartBytes` and `crypto.ChunkSize`.

  The `recorder` job of `ipcam-spike-recording.yml` runs them on Linux with `-race`, the `windows` job on windows-latest.

Re-apply on each adopted MediaMTX release: `agewriter.go` and `age_recipients.go` carry over as they are; redo the `NullRejecter` check in `jsonwrapper`'s `decode`, the two keys, their default and their validation in `conf/path.go`, the two settings in `recorder.go`, `recorder_instance.go` and `core/path.go`, the `.age` name in `closeCurPart`, the age writer in `create`, `endPart` in `writePartToDisk` and the age close in place of `writeDuration` in `finish`; then adapt `TestConfFromFile` and run the tests above. `doReloadConf` in `core/path.go` restarts the recorder only for the keys it compares, which the two MTX-2 keys are not: a new release that copies `recordAgeRecipients` or `recordAgePadLowBitrate` in `pathConfCanBeUpdated` must add them to that comparison too (the reload test catches it).

### MTX-3: segment-closed hook

- **What.**
  1. **The hook's start.** `recorder.OnSegmentCompleteFunc` becomes `func(path string, start time.Time, duration time.Duration)`. `start` is the segment's start: the wall time (NTP) of its first sample, the time that the file name encodes.
  2. **When it fires.** The fMP4 writer calls it once per segment, after MTX-1's rename and directory sync, with the final path. A segment whose close failed keeps its `.part` name and gets no call (MTX-1). It runs on MTX-1's disk writer, which creates the next segment's file only after it, so the hooks keep upstream's order: a segment's `OnSegmentComplete` before the next segment's `OnSegmentCreate`. The MPEG-TS writer passes its start too, because the type is shared; it fires as upstream's does.
  3. **The command's environment.** `internal/core/path.go` gives the `runOnRecordSegmentComplete` command `MTX_SEGMENT_START`, the start in Unix milliseconds, in decimal. It keeps upstream's variables: `MTX_PATH`, `MTX_SEGMENT_PATH` (now the final path), `MTX_SEGMENT_DURATION` (seconds, `strconv.FormatFloat(d.Seconds(), 'f', -1, 64)`), `RTSP_PATH`, `RTSP_PORT` and the `G1`… regexp groups. As upstream, `externalcmd` appends them to the environment of the MediaMTX process.
- **Why.** Ruling G05: the generated configuration sets `runOnRecordSegmentComplete` to `<ipcam-hub> hook segment-complete`, which forwards `{path, start, duration, …}` to the running `ipcam-hub`. Firing after the rename and the directory sync means that the catalog only learns of a segment whose final name is durable, and the start in milliseconds spares the hub from parsing it out of the file name.
- **Files touched.**
  - `internal/recorder/recorder.go` (the type and its default).
  - `internal/recorder/format_fmp4_segment.go` (the call in `finish`, after MTX-1's rename and directory sync).
  - `internal/recorder/format_mpegts_segment.go` (passes its start).
  - `internal/core/path.go` (`MTX_SEGMENT_START`).
  - Tests: `internal/recorder/mtx3_test.go`, `internal/core/mtx3_test.go`.
  - Upstream test adapted: `internal/recorder/recorder_test.go`, where the `OnSegmentComplete` functions of `TestRecorder` and `TestRecorderTimeDriftDetector` take the start.
- **Test.**
  - `TestMTX3_HookFiresAfterRenameWithFinalPath`: for a segment closed by the next segment's keyframe and for one closed when the recorder stops, the order is rename, directory sync, hook; the hook gets the rename's target, which exists, and a start within 1 ms of the wall time of the segment's first frame.
  - `TestMTX3_HookEnvironment` (`internal/core`): a MediaMTX core records an RTSP publisher, and its hook command (the test binary, as `TestMTX3_HookHelperProcess`) reports what it sees: `MTX_PATH`; `MTX_SEGMENT_PATH`, the only file left in the directory, which exists while its `.part` no longer does; `MTX_SEGMENT_START`, decimal and equal to the start in the file name, in milliseconds; `MTX_SEGMENT_DURATION`, equal to the file's `mvhd`; and a variable set in the parent environment.
- **Rebase status.** Applied on v1.21.1 (2026-10-20). Re-apply on each adopted MediaMTX release: the type change, the two writers' calls and the environment variable in `path.go`; then adapt the `OnSegmentComplete` functions in `recorder_test.go` and run the tests above.

### MTX-4: segment names in UTC

- **What.** The fMP4 recorder names a segment after its start in UTC: `closeCurPart` encodes `recordPath` with `startNTP.UTC()`, where upstream uses the zone of the clock that stamped the segment's first frame, the host's local time.
- **Why.** In the hour that repeats when daylight saving time ends (Romania: the last Sunday of October, 04:00 EEST back to 03:00 EET), a local name stands for two instants an hour apart, so reconcile, which reads a segment's start from its name, could place the rows and gaps of that hour an hour off. A UTC name stands for one instant. Running MediaMTX with `TZ=UTC` would do the same on Linux only: Go's `time.Local` ignores `TZ` on Windows (`time/zoneinfo_windows.go`, `initLocal` reads `GetTimeZoneInformation` alone, in Go 1.27.2), and the owner's PC runs Windows. The hub still sets `TZ=UTC` for its child, so that MediaMTX's log times are in the names' zone on Linux.
- **Files touched.**
  - `internal/recorder/format_fmp4_segment.go` (the start in UTC, in `closeCurPart`).
  - Test: `internal/recorder/mtx4_test.go`.
  - MTX-3's test adapted: `internal/core/mtx3_test.go` reads the name's start as UTC, since `recordstore.Path.Decode` reads a name without `%z` as local time.
- **Test.** `TestMTX4_SegmentNamedInUTC`: the segments whose first frames are stamped 03:30 EEST and 03:30 EET on 2026-10-25 are named `2026-10-25_00-30-00-000000.mp4` and `2026-10-25_01-30-00-000000.mp4`.
- **Rebase status.** Applied on v1.21.1 (2026-10-21). Re-apply on each adopted MediaMTX release: the `.UTC()` where `closeCurPart` encodes the segment's path, and the adaptation in `core/mtx3_test.go`; then run the tests above. The MPEG-TS recorder keeps upstream's local names: the hub records fMP4 only, as MTX-1 and MTX-2 do.

### Known interactions with the hub

What the patches leave to ipcam-hub's side (`hub/internal/recorder`), which MediaMTX's own features would otherwise break:

- **`.part` files and the record store.** `internal/recordstore`'s segment regexp is not anchored at the end, so the record cleaner and the playback server match `<name>.mp4.part` (and `.mp4.age.part`) as a segment. The configuration that the hub generates keeps `recordDeleteAfter` at 0, which turns the cleaner off, and the playback server and the control API off, so that nothing in MediaMTX reads or deletes a `.part` before the hub's reconcile repairs it. Retention belongs to the hub. Every other server is off too, MoQ included (§4.2). These three also read a segment name without `%z` as local time (`recordstore.Path.Decode`), while MTX-4 writes it in UTC: whoever turns one of them on must read the names as UTC first.
- **New directories.** MTX-1 syncs a segment's own directory only, and MediaMTX creates a missing one with `MkdirAll`, whose parents it never syncs. The hub creates each stream's directory and its date directories for today and tomorrow ahead of time, syncing the parent of each directory it creates.
- **Configuration reloads.** MediaMTX's file watcher ignores a change within 1 s of the last reload, and starts watching only after it has read its file. The hub spaces its writes by 1.1 s, and writes again once a starting MediaMTX watches its file.
- **The hook command's environment.** The hub's child gets no `MTX_` or `RTSP_` variable, which MediaMTX would read as configuration, and no value holding a secret key (C22); MediaMTX passes its environment, the hook's address and token included, to the hook command. Each child gets a new token, and `TZ=UTC`.
- **Stopping MediaMTX.** `internal/core/core.go` stops on `os.Interrupt` on every OS (and on `SIGTERM` on Linux): it closes its paths, whose recorders close their segments (rename, directory sync, hook), waits for the hook commands (`externalcmd.Pool.Close`) and exits. The hub sends `SIGTERM` on Linux. On Windows it starts MediaMTX in a process group of its own (`CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`) and sends `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` to that group, which Go delivers as `os.Interrupt`; it kills MediaMTX after 5 s. A hook command that is running when the Ctrl+Break comes gets it too, as a member of MediaMTX's group, so `ipcam-hub hook` catches the signals: on Windows, `signal.Ignore` would leave a Ctrl+Break to the default handler, which ends the process. A rebase must keep that shutdown path.
- **`.part` files left while MediaMTX runs.** The hub repairs a `.part` without waiting for its next start in two cases: when the child has exited, and when a newer `.part` of the same path has appeared (a failed write or fsync makes the recorder close the segment under its `.part` name and start again in the same process, MTX-1). The second case relies on MediaMTX closing a path's segment file before it creates that path's next one: MTX-1's disk writer creates a segment's file only once the segment before has finished its close (`finish`: rename, directory sync and hook, or a failure that leaves the `.part`), a failing recorder instance waits in `formatFMP4.close` until its disk writer has closed every segment, before `Recorder.run` starts the next instance, and `pathManager.doClosePath` waits for the old path (`pa.wait()`) before a reload creates it again. A rebase must keep that order, or the hub would repair a file that MediaMTX still writes; `TestMTX1_SlowSegmentCloseKeepsRecording` checks the first, with the close held for as long as a slow disk holds it. That is why the next segment's parts wait in memory during a slow close, rather than in a new `.part` (MTX-1, 5.).
